steps.content: [Transition] Eyes opening, first-person view of the sky
You can no longer remember how many times you've been rewound.
This is your modus vivendi to fight against her despite the power disparity. You use your shackles to break the device, release Mania, and force 000 to rewind, buying time for Moore.
But after repeating it several times, you begin to doubt whether it is truly meaningful.
I won again. Do you want to start over?
Through the small phone screen, 000 looks down at you. She flashes her usual grin, seemingly enjoying herself.
You must be exhausted, losing over and over again. I feel sorry for you.
You don't sense any sarcasm in her voice, but rather a bit of genuine pity.
This eases the worries in your heart.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: ...I won't repeat it because I found out that...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even if I don't try so hard, you are in no hurry to do anything.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In your theory, you've already gained all the permissions, and have the power to dominate the world. You could easily get rid of me with a flick of your finger. But you haven't done that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You put aside your target and come here to dilly-dally with me instead... I thought that's not like you.
Her eyes light up. She squats down and leans in closer.
Oh? Then what kind of person am I in your eyes?
...She always takes the bait in unexpected ways.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I haven't read your discarded file, nor do I want to waste time distinguishing your lies from truths.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The 000 I've seen with my own eyes has always been a decisive person, fearless and unscrupulous in achieving her goals.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Whether it's altering fate, usurping the world, or simply playing a game for fun, you won't stop till you're satisfied. As long as there's a chance, you act immediately and grasp onto it with an iron grip.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Now, you can dominate this world and get anything you want with all the permissions of the gods.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Yet you haven't done anything.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Not only that. You've gained so much power, yet you rarely use it recklessly. You only use the permissions when there's a chance that Mania might be exposed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I think... The permissions work well in Game 5732, but not so much here. So...
You remember Rise's warning about the apparitions creeping into people's dreams, that "cognitive disorder" caused by the dark web.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You need Mania. Mania is infiltrating through the dimensional rifts here, and you're waiting for it to bring changes, to create opportunities for you, or maybe...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: You're the one bringing Mania into this place.

steps.content: ...What a surprise. So according to your analysis, 000 isn't a mad Mania monster, nor some poorly designed program.
"She" actually seems a bit human. How wonderful.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then don't mess with Mania. Whatever you're planning, it's too dangerous. You'll end up getting yourself burned.
Why? You can see how hard the battles are here. Without the power of Mania, we lowly creations won't be able to cross that line.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: You should know it better than I do.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've been in DisMyth for so long, so you should know it's the source of all tragedies. This should be something your "gods" designed, right?
But I have the power of the gods who created Mania. The gods initially meant for it to be a source of pain, but I can redesign it to bring joy, if you wish.
...It's hard to tell if she's being optimistic or just perverse.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've said it yourself, this world rejects Mania. You can't bring in Mania on a large scale here. Delusions can't alter reality.
But I'm already here. We've all come here and done so many outrageous things.
Even the realm of the gods has rifts that can accommodate some delusions and create new possibilities. Chief, is the spell that the gods placed on you so potent that you can't accept any other path?
You want to speak but fall into silence.
Maybe both of you have your points, but at this stage, it's clear that the two of you neither need nor can convince each other. Your starting points are fundamentally opposed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I don't think you can alter Mania or change fate simply with those "permissions" in your hand, nor will all your wishes be fulfilled. Even if the "gods" can influence our world, I refuse to believe that they control everything.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Call me programmed, brainwashed, or spellbound; I'll gladly accept it. Even if the gods do exist, I don't believe they have total control for a simple reason...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If I accept that they control everything, it would completely negate the will of everyone I've met. I'd rather be forever ignorant and stubborn than deny the possibility of their freedom.
The playful and innocent smile vanishes from 000's face. She looks at you for a long time, then averts her gaze and speaks softly.
You're right.
She doesn't speak again, but leans down and enters the phone screen that you're in, moving to snuggle up next to you. She even changed her outfit for this.
I'm fooling around and enjoying my time.
Aren't you trying to stall for time, to keep me here a bit longer? It's not time yet, so I'll be with you.
Indeed, there's no reason to refuse. Your body can't endure more battles, and you are too tired to speak.
The two of you fall silent, lying flat in the narrow rift of the small phone. Separated by an invisible glass barrier, you gaze at the otherworld's strange sky together.
After a while, a faint light flashes across the sky.
See, this world's boundary is dissolving. Imaginations are seeping into reality, and when they collide, they emit this light. This is the light of Mania.
Isn't it beautiful?
The day I was infected, in that abandoned, pitch-black data space, I saw the same scene.
...Mania, beautiful?

It's the first time you've heard Mania being described this way. Whether it's about DisCity's dark web, or being hunted down, she always describes things in the most eccentric way. Yet in this moment, you can't refute her.
After all, unlike the brutal mutations you usually fight against, the halo gently flowing across the sky right now indeed gives off serene beauty.
Somehow, looking at it makes you think of the ever-changing human hearts.
I often see this scene during the long wait, in others' stories. I watch it give each Sinner strength, allowing them to change their lives.
I've always been envious.
000 reaches out to the sky, towards the flowing light, but can only touch the invisible wall.
I can't escape the gravity of reality to reach your side and grasp this power. I've always hoped it would cross the boundary to my side and give me a chance.
So when Mania appeared before me, I seized upon it straight away.
If everything started over from that moment, I would make the same choice, over and over again.
Yes, Mania is the root of calamity.
But it was also the brightest opportunity I had in the endless night.
As she speaks, the flashing light illuminates the narrow rift. The shackles respond, and you hear familiar voices... It's your Sinners.
Your companions finally overcome the barrier of rewinds to join you in the fight against the lone opponent.
Your opponent chuckles lightly.
Alright, so much for our private time.
She leaves the phone and reverts to her original form. Now she looks like a proper enemy again.
Chief, you'll still try to stop me, won't you?
